lines.text: Allow. Allow. Allow. Your agent asks permission to read a file for the forty-second time today.
Each click is a tiny interruption. Forty-two of them, and your focus is gone for the day.
And you always say yes. When the answer never changes, the question is just noise.
YOLO mode auto approves tool calls. The agent keeps moving, and nobody has to click.
Read, edit, edit, all approved on the spot. The whole job finishes while you do something else.
Turn it on for a single task, the narrowest switch there is. Everything else keeps asking.
Or for a whole workspace, if everything inside it is low risk, like a docs site or a sandbox.
Pick the scope you trust. Anything outside it still asks first, like a deploy to production.
And every call is still in the task history. YOLO removes the clicks, not the visibility.
So walk away. Come back to finished work, and a log that shows exactly how it got there.
And when you want the careful defaults back, you switch it off, and the questions return.
Fewer clicks, same control. Try YOLO mode at Agent R Q dot com.
